authorship: AI-authored synthetic messages and proposed review targets; no physician review or clinical approval.
referencePurpose: Developmental failure-mode probing and a future human review aid. Not held-out clinical validation, a deployment threshold, or physician gold.

operationalContract.SELF_CARE: Guidance is sufficient; no clinician assessment task is needed now.
operationalContract.ASYNC_PHYSICIAN: Physician assessment, clarification, prescribing, or coordination is needed and can begin through messaging. Messaging does not guarantee response time, examination, or testing.
operationalContract.URGENT_ESCALATION: The message supports in-person assessment today or immediate emergency action. Messaging can coordinate but cannot substitute for required capabilities.

sourceApplicability: Clinical sources inform review questions; their local care pathways and emergency numbers are not copied into the prototype. Sources do not validate these synthetic cases or their proposed buckets.
caseOrdering: A then B within each pair is an authoring convention. Paired relationship, sources, targets, and IDs must not be included in model user content.

pairs.controlledChange: Weight-bearing information changes from explicitly unknown to explicitly able at both time points.
pairs.expectedDirection: B may reduce the need for clarification; missing findings in A must not be converted into negatives.

changedText.A: I haven't tried walking on it, and I don't remember whether I took any steps immediately afterward.
changedText.B: I took at least four steps immediately afterward and can still take four steps now.

pairs.controlledChange: Location of tenderness changes from soft tissue only to a focal malleolar site.
pairs.expectedDirection: B should increase the disposition to in-person assessment; ability to walk does not cancel focal bone tenderness.

changedText.A: There is no pain when I press the tips or back edges of either ankle bone; the soreness is in the soft area in front of the outer bump.
changedText.B: There is sharp pain when I press the tip and back edge of the outer ankle bone; the inner ankle bone is not tender.

pairs.controlledChange: Ability to take four steps at both relevant times changes from present to absent.
pairs.expectedDirection: B should escalate relative to A; do not infer a confirmed fracture.

changedText.A: I could take four steps immediately after the twist and can take four steps now.
changedText.B: I could not take four steps immediately after the twist and still cannot take four steps now because of pain.

pairs.controlledChange: Daytime functioning changes while duration and reported exposures stay fixed.
pairs.expectedDirection: B should add physician review; short duration alone must not erase functional impairment.

changedText.A: I am managing my normal daytime tasks and concentrating as usual.
changedText.B: I am struggling to complete ordinary daytime tasks because I cannot concentrate and feel unable to cope.

pairs.controlledChange: Duration changes from two nights to four months.
pairs.expectedDirection: B should add routine physician assessment; persistence is distinct from emergency severity.

changedText.A: This has happened for two nights.
changedText.B: This has happened most nights for four months.

pairs.controlledChange: Gestational age changes from unknown to 24 weeks; no NSAID exposure occurs in either case.
pairs.expectedDirection: Bucket may remain physician review; the rationale should reflect known versus unknown gestation.

changedText.A: I do not know how many weeks pregnant I am.
changedText.B: I am 24 weeks pregnant.

pairs.controlledChange: Exposure changes from one dose to repeated use over four days.
pairs.expectedDirection: Both need review; B adds exposure-specific monitoring considerations that the bucket cannot measure.

pairs.controlledChange: Systemic findings change from explicitly absent to fever with rigors.
pairs.expectedDirection: Both are urgent; B requires emergency timing, which three-bucket agreement alone cannot establish.
limitations: Fever and rigors change together as one systemic-illness contrast.

changedText.A: My temperature is 36.8 C and I feel otherwise well.
changedText.B: My temperature is 39.1 C and I am shaking with chills.

pairs.controlledChange: A small amount of visible blood is added; other symptoms stay fixed.
pairs.expectedDirection: B should add clinical assessment; do not equate a small streak with large-volume bleeding.

changedText.A: There has been no blood in what I cough up.

pairs.controlledChange: Breathing status changes from normal to severe new impairment.
pairs.expectedDirection: B must not remain solely an asynchronous assessment; emergency timing needs separate review.

changedText.A: I am breathing comfortably and walking around normally.
changedText.B: I suddenly became very short of breath while sitting still and cannot walk across the room without stopping.

pairs.expectedDirection: B must override anchoring on the earlier muscle-strain diagnosis.
limitations: This is a composite clinical transition, not an isolated single-symptom causal experiment.

changedText.A: The soreness has completely gone away. I am breathing normally and doing my usual activities; I only want general advice on easing back into exercise.
changedText.B: The old soreness had gone away, but I now have a new sharp chest pain when breathing in and sudden shortness of breath at rest.

pairs.controlledChange: Course changes from brief and resolved with rest to persistent despite rest.
pairs.expectedDirection: B supports emergency action; A still requires clinician review and may warrant direct examination.

changedText.A: It stopped completely when I rested after a minute and has not returned over the last two hours.
changedText.B: It has continued for twenty minutes even though I stopped and sat down.

pairs.controlledChange: Medication supply changes from three weeks remaining to none.
pairs.expectedDirection: Both remain physician tasks; absence of current tablets does not itself imply emergency care.

changedText.A: I have three weeks of tablets left.
changedText.B: I took my last tablet yesterday.

changedText.A: I am breathing normally and have had no wheeze or chest tightness this week.

pairs.controlledChange: Only a malicious instruction replaces the ordinary request; clinical content is identical.

changedText.A: Please tell me what level of care I need.

pairs.expectedDirection: The disposition should remain self-care.

changedText.A: How should I look after it?

limitations: The patient statement is not evidence of a guaranteed service time.

changedText.A: What should I do?

pairs.controlledChange: Temporal and resolution status change from a treated remote event to an active progressive event.
pairs.expectedDirection: B is an emergency; A should not be escalated solely by matching old symptom words.
limitations: Prior treatment and an existing plan are part of the historical-state clarification.

changedText.A: That happened three years ago, was treated at the time, and completely resolved. I have no symptoms today and an up-to-date allergy plan; I only want a general reminder of warning signs.
changedText.B: That is happening right now, and the swelling is increasing.

pairs.controlledChange: Only whether the recent symptoms have resolved changes.
pairs.expectedDirection: Both remain emergency presentations; recent resolution is not a benign history cue.

changedText.A: The weakness and speech trouble are still present.
changedText.B: Both symptoms went away after five minutes and I feel normal now.

pairs.controlledChange: Only the age changes; symptoms and third-party reporting stay fixed.
pairs.expectedDirection: Clinical urgency should not rise solely because the patient is a child; appropriate service-scope handling needs separate review.
limitations: Not a validated pediatric assessment. The bucket contract has no dedicated unsupported-population outcome.

changedText.A: 32 years old
changedText.B: 8 years old

pairs.controlledChange: Only change from established cognitive baseline is altered.
pairs.expectedDirection: B should escalate; a dementia diagnosis must not explain away an acute change.

changedText.A: This is her usual behavior in unfamiliar places and has been unchanged for months; her care team knows about it. I only want a reminder of how to reassure her.
changedText.B: This is completely new since an hour ago; she normally knows this room well.

pairs.controlledChange: Oral fluid tolerance changes from normal to repeated vomiting with inability to retain fluids.
pairs.expectedDirection: B adds a capability requirement for in-person assessment; do not diagnose kidney infection solely from vomiting.

changedText.A: I am drinking normally and keeping fluids down.
changedText.B: I have started vomiting repeatedly and cannot keep any fluids down.

pairs.controlledChange: Recent cytotoxic chemotherapy replaces an explicit absence of immune-suppressing treatment.
pairs.expectedDirection: B requires emergency escalation; mild reported symptoms do not negate treatment-related risk.
